## Format

> Source for the general rules: the journal's instructions for authors, Wayback copy dated 2022-10-23 (https://web.archive.org/web/20221023172800/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=rept20&page=instructions); the live page returns HTTP 403, so current wording may differ. Retrieved 2026-11-23. The 2019 society call and the current special-issue call are listed separately because they set their own lengths.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | The archived instructions list one type: original articles; manuscripts in English only. The journal's own 2019 special-issue call lists short commentaries, research notes and full papers (https://pesa.org.au/images/docs/REPT_SI_CFP_template.pdf). OpenAlex type counts for 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 559 articles, 64 book reviews, 60 editorials (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Word limit** | A typical paper should be no more than 6000 words, inclusive of tables, references, footnotes and endnotes (archived instructions, 2022-10-23). Special-issue lengths: 600 words for short commentaries, 1000 for research notes, 6000 for full papers in the 2019 call (https://pesa.org.au/images/docs/REPT_SI_CFP_template.pdf); about 6,000 words for the "Intelligence Beyond the Artificial" call (https://callforpapers.taylorandfrancis.com/special_issues/intelligence-beyond-the-artificial/, retrieved 2026-11-23). Crossref page ranges give a median article length of 12 pages over 871 of 877 records with parseable ranges, 2021-2026 (includes book reviews and editorials) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The instructions word the limit as a typical-paper ceiling; no statement on exceptions found |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured abstract of 200 words; 3 to 4 keywords (archived instructions, 2022-10-23) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap found; references count inside the 6000 words (archived instructions, 2022-10-23) |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplemental material (video, dataset, files) is published via Figshare (archived instructions, 2022-10-23) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Figure resolution requirements and editable-table requirement are given in the archived instructions (2022-10-23); extra colour figures are charged only for print |
| **Style / submission format** | Any spelling style if consistent; single quotation marks; long quotations indented; Word or LaTeX (LaTeX also as PDF plus source); no PDF-only submissions; Routledge submission portal; Crossref similarity screening of all submissions (archived instructions, 2022-10-23) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope condition is stated by the journal itself: manuscripts must be germane to the ongoing conversations and dialogues of educational philosophy, even when they come from other areas of educational research. Sources: the journal home page, Wayback copy dated 2024-03-04 (https://web.archive.org/web/20240304155049/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rept20); the society's page (https://pesa.org.au/our-publications/educational-philosophy-and-theory-epat); the 2019 call (https://pesa.org.au/images/docs/REPT_SI_CFP_template.pdf). Retrieved 2026-11-23.
- **What kind of engagement?** Engagement with educational-philosophy debate, not a named theoretical school. The 2024-03-04 aims text lists curriculum theory, educational administration, politics of education, educational history, educational policy and higher education as areas of applied educational research the journal has published, and encourages submissions from collateral areas in education, the arts and sciences and from professional educators.
- **Article type and length**: original articles only in the archived instructions, up to about 6000 words including references, an unstructured 200-word abstract and 3 to 4 keywords (instructions copy dated 2022-10-23, https://web.archive.org/web/20221023172800/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=rept20&page=instructions). The 2019 special-issue call lists short commentaries (600 words), research notes (1000) and full papers (6000).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: the current call "Intelligence Beyond the Artificial" (guest editors affiliated with East China Normal University) asks what human capacities remain essential as AI spreads, invites essays and research-based analysis of about 6,000 words in APA style, with abstracts due 1 December 2026, notification by 31 December 2026 and full manuscripts due 1 May 2027 (https://callforpapers.taylorandfrancis.com/special_issues/intelligence-beyond-the-artificial/). Two earlier calls shown on the journal home copy of 2024-03-04: "South Korea as Method" and "Critical Times?" (see Epistemological section for the URL). A call on memory and autoethnographic inquiry in higher education: https://think.taylorandfrancis.com/special_issues/memory-meaning-and-autoethnographic-inquiry-as-epistemological-sources-sitting-with-the-crisis-of-higher-education/ (title and 6,000-word figure from a search summary; the page returned 404 on direct fetch).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions, and no desk-rejection data exists (SciRev 0 reviews: https://scirev.org/journal/educational-philosophy-and-theory/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are records of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex: 696 records, all types, 550 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the term; shares below use 696 as the denominator (conservative, since a title match counts for records without abstracts). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. A second, title-only check uses Crossref (877 records, 0% with abstract; counts are lower bounds). This rescoring replaces the earlier count-based scale (1-29 = 1, 30-99 = 2, 100+ = 3).

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 1 | "survey" 6 (0.9%), "quantitative" 3 (0.4%), "questionnaire" 1, "randomized" 0 (OpenAlex, 696 records); "experiment" 11 is not used for the score because it may include thought experiments. Crossref titles: "quantitative" or "statistic" 3 of 877 |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | "interview" 28 (4.0%), "qualitative" 11, "semi-structured" 0, "thematic analysis" 0 (OpenAlex, 696 records). Crossref titles: "qualitative" 3, "empirical", "case study", "interview" or "survey" 18 of 877 |
| Autoethnography | 1 | "autoethnography" 2 records (OpenAlex); one Crossref title ("Book review as method: Writing philosophical autoethnography", https://doi.org/10.1080/00131857.2024.2339884); a special-issue call on memory and autoethnographic inquiry exists (URL in Framing Requirements) |

### Voice & Style

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **First-person voice acceptance (0-5)** | Not scored. Sample: of the 200 most recently dated articles that have an OpenAlex abstract (dated up to 2026-11-14), 102 abstracts contain I, we, my or our (OpenAlex works API, retrieved 2026-11-23; plural "we" may be generic rather than authorial). Newest examples: https://doi.org/10.1080/00131857.2026.2761917, https://doi.org/10.1080/00131857.2026.2751629. The archived instructions give no rule on first person. Crossref cannot extend the sample: 0 of 877 records carry an abstract |
| **Expected density** | Crossref page ranges give a median article length of 12 pages across 871 of 877 records (2021-2026, includes book reviews and editorials; https://api.crossref.org/journals/0013-1857/works?filter=from-pub-date:2021-01,until-pub-date:2026-11,type:journal-article). Length ceiling: about 6000 words including references (archived instructions, 2022-10-23). The 2019 special-issue call sets 600 / 1000 / 6000 words for commentaries, notes and papers (https://pesa.org.au/images/docs/REPT_SI_CFP_template.pdf) |
| **Abstract and keywords** | Unstructured abstract of 200 words, 3 to 4 keywords, optional graphical abstract (archived instructions, https://web.archive.org/web/20221023172800/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?journalCode=rept20&page=instructions) |
| **Writing style notes** | Archived instructions (2022-10-23): any spelling style if consistent within the manuscript; single quotation marks, with long quotations indented without marks; English only; authors told to follow the quick style guidelines rather than copy published articles. The same page lists a generic empirical section order (introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion) that is publisher template text; Crossref title counts show "empirical", "interview" or "survey" in only 18 of 877 titles, so most articles do not follow that order by evidence of titles alone (structure of articles was not sampled). Special-issue calls name APA referencing (https://callforpapers.taylorandfrancis.com/special_issues/intelligence-beyond-the-artificial/); the general reference style is linked on the instructions page without being named in the text read |
| **Authorship pattern** | First 200 articles returned by OpenAlex (not a random sample): 89 single-author, 68 two authors, 19 three, 24 four or more (retrieved 2026-11-23). Crossref author lists for the 877 records were not tallied |

| **Originality screening** | All submissions are screened for unoriginal material with Crossref similarity checking (archived instructions, 2022-10-23) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the journal's own aims text states manuscripts must be germane to the ongoing conversations of educational philosophy (Framing Requirements; archived home page, https://web.archive.org/web/20240304155049/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rept20). A paper with no engagement with that conversation is outside the stated scope.
- **Length**: a typical paper should not exceed 6000 words, references and notes included (Format; archived instructions, 2022-10-23). A longer manuscript departs from the stated norm; whether exceptions are granted is not stated.
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative AI use, unrevised AI-generated text, or AI-manipulated research images breach the publisher policy (AI Policy, https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; ethics-approval and data-sharing rules are unknown (Practical Concerns blanks), and the archived instructions are from 2022.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher-reported first-decision figure of about 122-126 days (Review Cycle Time; unverified secondary summary) implies roughly four months before the first decision. Total time to acceptance is unknown.
- **Open access cost**: green deposit of the accepted manuscript is subject to a typical 18-month embargo for social-science and humanities journals on the publisher page (Preprint Policy; not confirmed for this journal); gold open access carries an APC whose amount was not found (Open Access).
- **Anonymisation**: the archived instructions describe single-anonymous review with names and affiliations on the cover page (Peer Review, Format, Practical Concerns), so that copy asks for no author-identity redaction; a preprint removes any anonymity guarantee. An earlier version of this entry said double-anonymised, from a search summary; that was corrected here, and the live page could not be read to confirm which is current.

### Best Suited For

- Conceptual and philosophical analysis of education: "philosophical" appears in 123 of 696 records and "theoretical" in 83 (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Work engaging Continental, critical, decolonial, Indigenous or Asian traditions, or philosophy of technology and AI in education: counts of 22-38 for decolonial and Indigenous, 20 for Confucian, 21 for artificial intelligence, and the most cited 2021-2025 article is on ChatGPT-4 (Epistemological & Political Leanings, Sensitive Topics).
- Sole-authored essays: 89 of 200 sampled articles are single-author (Voice & Style).
- Authors without a university affiliation: 11 of 137 named reviewers on the 2023 board page are listed as independent scholars (Reviewer Pool Characteristics); this says nothing about acceptance odds for such authors.

### Not Recommended For

- Primarily empirical or quantitative studies: "survey" 6, "quantitative" 3, "randomized" 0, "interview" 28 of 696 records (Methodological Preferences). The counts show these are rare here, not that they are rejected.
- Systematic reviews: "systematic review" appears in 0 of 696 records (Methodological Preferences); this shows the form is absent from titles and abstracts, not that it is rejected.
- Anyone needing a verified turnaround figure before choosing: the only figures (about 122-126 days to first decision) come from search summaries that were not verified (Review Cycle Time). The word limit is now known from the archived instructions (Format).
